excerpts.text: A REST API is a web service that exposes resources at URLs and lets clients act on them with standard HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT and DELETE, with each result reported as a status code such as 200 or 404.

A REST API uses the HTTP method to say what to do with the resource at the URL. RFC 9110, the HTTP Semantics standard published in June 2022, calls a method safe when its semantics are essentially read-only, and idempotent when several identical requests have the same intended effect on the server as one.

| POST | Submits data, often causing a change or side effect | No | No | Only with explicit freshness information |
| PUT | Replaces the resource with the request content | No | Yes | No |
| PATCH | Applies a partial modification | No | No | Only with explicit freshness information |

assessment.rationale: Spans 26 and 34 define idempotent per RFC 9110: 'several identical requests have the same intended effect'. Span 39 says a repeated POST can create two orders, showing POST is not idempotent. The claim that safe methods are idempotent contradicts this.
assessment.provenance_note: RFC 9110 defines idempotent; source gives POST counterexample.
